# Background

## Project and repository aims
The basis of this project is rooted in the work done in the masters thesis by Brøten [-@broten_crabs_2026]. The aim of the project was improving the monitoring of the data-limited Brown crab (*Cancer pagurus*) stock in Norway with machine learning and underwater video surveys. 

The aim of creating this repositry is not to push innvoation or show excellence in coding but rather the opposite and make machine learning algorithms more approachable for marine scientists in fisheris application.



The brown crab stock in Norway (despite its large distribution there is little genetic variation for it to be assumed to be more than one stock) lacks a formal stock assessment due to a multitude of reasons, one of them being a data-deficity primarily from the 
In Norwegian waters the brown crabs distribution spans across 10 degrees of latitude (kilde, bakke et al), and traditional methods 

using the underutilized resource of underwater video from surveys and coastal monitoring programs from the Insitute of Marine Research

Where the general idea was that coastal monitoring programs and mulitple surveys at the Institue of Marine Research applied video surveys to monitor coastal habitats.

## About the repository

This repository uses the same codes, functions & packages used in the masters thesis to obtain the results.

To start trying on your own, you can easily clone this repository on your own computer, or preferably on a server with a high GPU.


# Before running the scripts

## Prerequisites

Need to have Python installed. `raw_to_yolo.ipynb` will check for missing packages and install them automatically (see "Chunk 0").

Ideally a server if you want to train your own model.

If you want to create your own crab-detector, then you'll need an annotated training dataset. Where the annotations are stored in a folder called annotations, with two folders, images/default (here all the images live) and 

### Data

The repo only ships a small example/test dataset (`data/annotations/test_annotations`) so the scripts can be run and verified without downloading everything.

The full training dataset (~8,000 images) used in the original masters project is hosted externally: **[LINK TO ADD]**. Download it and point `CONFIG["ANNOTATIONS_FILE"]` / `CONFIG["IMAGES_DIR"]` in `raw_to_yolo.ipynb` at the local copy to reproduce the full training run.
